title: Family trees of ten species
hook: Ten species could be related in many ways. How many family trees are there?

knows: species can be related in a branching family tree
doesNotKnow: that the number of possible trees explodes with the number of species

misconception: With 10 species, one can check all possible family trees.
objective: The learner can explain that each added species can join any branch, 2k - 1 places for a tree of k species, so the count multiplies: 3 x 5 x 7 x ... x 17 = 34,459,425 trees for 10 species.

claims.text: The number of rooted, binary (two branches at each fork) trees on n labelled species is (2n - 3)!! = 1 x 3 x 5 x ... x (2n - 3).
claims.source: Felsenstein, Inferring Phylogenies, 2004, ch. 3 (number of possible trees); Schroeder 1870 (Schroder's first problem).

claims.text: A rooted tree of k species has 2k - 1 branches (counting the stub above the root), so the next species can join in 2k - 1 places; this gives 1 tree for 2 species, 3 for 3, 15 for 4, 105 for 5 and 34,459,425 for 10.
claims.source: trees(k+1) = trees(k) x (2k - 1); artifacts/scratch/w5life/trees.mjs gives 17!! = 34,459,425 for 10 species. Demo.tsx computes the count from places(k).

claims.text: Model (stated on the stage and in the reveal): only rooted, branching trees with two branches at each fork are counted; which branch each species joins in the picture is a seeded illustration (mulberry32 seed 5) and does not change the count.
claims.source: Model choice in Demo.tsx; brief life #50.

recall.question: A tree of 5 species has 9 branches. In how many places can a 6th species join it?
recall.why: A new species can join on any branch, and each choice gives a different tree; that is why the number of trees multiplies as species are added.
